findings.obligation: nw-code-craftsmanship rule 33 (no repeated I/O a path does not need) with nw-code-design-oo rule 7 (no element no accepted outcome reads in that state): a read whose answer cannot change the page is work the page does not need.
findings.observation: answer() calls live_opener() unconditionally, so every render of the instance integrations page and every post that answers it issues an extra SELECT ... FOR UPDATE over integration_replica_states (crates/foundry-store/src/integrations/instance.rs:1154). The only consumer of that fact is UnopenableOffer::of_gate in page_state (handlers/instance.rs:693), and UnopenableOffer::decide returns RestoreOnly for every mode but KeyMode::Unopenable (secrets_key_rotation.rs:177-184), so in the Sealed, Direct, AwaitingSecretsKey and NoInstanceKey modes - the states the page is in almost all of the time - the row read and the FOR UPDATE lock it takes change nothing the admin reads. The ReadOnlyDoor type already models this read as door-specific (PageRead::ReplicaStates is listed only for SecretsKeyStartOver, handlers/instance.rs:556), and answer() reads it outside that list for every mode. reviewer_reason: measured by reading the call graph at the reviewed commit, not by a profile; no latency requirement is breached and no accepted outcome is wrong, which is why this does not block.
findings.remediation: Read the replica states only where the answer can be used: guard the live_opener() call in answer() on the state in which UnopenableOffer can be anything but RestoreOnly (integrations.key_mode() == KeyMode::Unopenable), or let the one owner decide by giving the instance page its own PageRead list as the other doors have, so the page and the start-over door keep reading one answer.

findings.obligation: Accepted authority ADR-IIS-SKR-001 Decision: the typed confirmation is a StartOverConfirmation value the apply cannot be called without; with the consumed design docs/feature/iis-secrets-key-replace/architecture.md:44, :391-393 (StartOverConfirmation::typed(field) -> Option<StartOverConfirmation>), :997-1005 (its owning module, its only constructor, and the start-over POST handler that cannot call the apply without the value), :1132 and :1704; plus nw-type-level-design write rules 3 and 4 (a decision returns its evidence, no bare boolean where the caller needs a witness; an operation that accepts only validated input takes the evidence type) and nw-code-craftsmanship rule 39 (a document the change touches agrees with the code).
findings.observation: No StartOverConfirmation exists anywhere in the candidate: argv grep -rn StartOverConfirmation --include=*.rs over crates/ and xtask/ prints nothing, exit 1, while the same grep over docs/ prints the ADR Decision line, four architecture.md lines and handoff.json:593. What ships instead is UnopenableOffer::confirms(typed: &str) -> bool at secrets_key_rotation.rs:206, checked once as a guard at secrets_key.rs:405, after which started_over(&state, &store, user.user_id) and through it InstanceKeyWrites::start_over_secrets_key carry no evidence of the confirmation at all: the apply is callable from anywhere in the module with no confirmation in sight, which is the state the design excluded by construction. The design claim at architecture.md:1704, that the exclusion is the StartOverConfirmation constructor which rustc enforces at the call of the apply, is false against these bytes, and the same diff ships that document. No scope amendment covers it: the S3 Records authorise the plan_generate reuse and the KeyOffer extension but hold no entry for the confirmation carrier, and craft.S3.json declares no deviation for it. reviewer_reason: a construction and document-fidelity gap, not a behaviour gap. The public refusal of a wrong, empty and lower-case Confirmation is observed green at the driving port (feature lines 1414-1456) in the 29/29 lane run of observation R9, which is why it does not block.
findings.remediation: Add the carrier the design names to crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/secrets_key_rotation.rs: StartOverConfirmation with StartOverConfirmation::typed(field: &str) -> Option<StartOverConfirmation> as its only constructor, holding the trim-and-compare now in confirms; remove the boolean validator left beside the evidence path; and make started_over and the start-over write take the value, so rustc refuses an apply without it. If the human amends the scope to keep a boolean guard instead, correct ADR-IIS-SKR-001 and architecture.md:44, :391-393, :997-1005, :1132 and :1704 in the same change, with the amendment and its provenance recorded, so no shipped document claims a guarantee the code does not give.

Role-owned assessment of every logical implementation unit of the candidate, on cohesion and invariant ownership, semantic reuse, dependency direction, type precision and effect separation. The ten units are: (1) Store::replace_secrets_key with ReplaceOutcome and replace_stored_key - one locked transaction, compare-and-set on the stored key id, the shipped reseal_sealed_values walk reused rather than a second walk, every refusal path rolling back before the canary, the activity line and the version bump (crates/foundry-store/src/integrations/instance.rs:474-520, 1203-1230); (2) Store::start_over_secrets_key with StartOverOutcome, read_replica_states and discard_sealed_credentials - the gate read inside the same locked transaction, which is what makes the falsifier 'checks the gate only at the GET' unreachable (:521-567, 1154-1175, 1232-1265); (3) the two Activity arms with their wire names and the two activity_line renderings, added to the one closed set (instance.rs:374-398, handlers/instance.rs:817-825); (4) the InstanceKeyWrites port with replace_secrets_key, start_over_secrets_key and replica_states, its StoreCapabilities implementation and the LiveReplicaGate alias - every test double of the trait extended with unreachable! arms rather than a silent default (store_capabilities.rs:218-290, 493-560); (5) secrets_key_rotation.rs - SavedCredentials owning the I-22 count and the I-23/I-24/I-28 forms, LiveOpeners owning the beat window with the injected clock, UnopenableOffer owning the three I-26 states and the confirmation words, ReplacePlan owning what a replacement stores and carrying no Debug; (6) keys.rs KeyMode::replaces and GeneratePlan::reseal_under, with the shipped reseal delegating to it so one reading remains (keys.rs:126-170); (7) handlers/secrets_key.rs - KeyOffer as the third arm of the shipped offer type, the read-only replace and start-over pages, replaced/written and started_over; (8) handlers/instance.rs - PageFacts.live_opener, PageRead::ReplicaStates inside the type whose every variant is a read, the two ReadOnlyDoor arms, gate_of, the two SavedNotice arms with the counted wire name, and page_state deciding all three I-26 states so no template decides; (9) IntegrationSettings::key_wrapper; (10) the two routes, the two templates, the module exports and the check_arch fence data. Judgment: cohesion and ownership hold - each fact has one owner (the count, the gate, the offer, the wrapper, the plan), dependencies point inward through InstanceKeyWrites with no vendor type crossing it, no domain decision sits in a template or in SQL, the outcome of every operation is a named enum variant and no domain outcome is a null or an exception, and the only mutable state is inside the locked store transactions. Type precision: ReplaceOutcome<E>, StartOverOutcome, ReplaceAnswer, StartOverAnswer, StartOverCost, UnopenableOffer and SavedCredentials make the wrong state unconstructible at every boundary the design names; the one invariant not carried in a type is the caller-side I-26 condition of discard_sealed_credentials, now stated in three docs and in the fence comment. Object Calisthenics in domain and application code: no anemic entity, no application transaction script holding a domain decision, no getter-driven decision, primitives wrapped where they carry domain meaning. Refactoring Priority Premise, every level scanned: no dead code, no misplaced responsibility, and the duplication and the primitive-obsession smells the earlier round found are gone; no lower-level smell is left hiding a higher one.

Oracle completeness against the original Request, inspected stimulus by stimulus in the executable oracle rather than from the acceptance prose. The Request has five demanded behaviours. (a) The admin replaces the key from the instance integrations page through GET then POST of /admin/instance/integrations/secrets-key/replace: feature lines 1069-1105 drive the control on the page, the confirm page, I-23 with its count of 3, the apply, the landing address with no notice, the stored key read as a new one through the key test seam, and the activity line in full; the outline at 1114-1131 drives all four I-23 counts and asserts the page changed nothing, the outline at 1134-1151 drives all three I-24 counts. (b) Every stored credential, the saved Slack app included, sealed again under the new key with nobody reconnecting: observed at 1101-1105 by the saved Slack connection still opening, the connection not marked lost, no workspace admin emailed, and a new issue of Sam reaching both the Slack channel and the Matrix room after the replacement; and across replicas at 1167-1181. (c) A failed re-seal changes nothing: the acceptance record declares P3 NotTested at the public port with a justification I checked - no public door can make the sealing closure refuse - and assigns both halves as completion obligations, which are met by executed tests, crates/foundry-store/tests/iis_instance_store.rs::a_refused_replacement_and_a_lost_compare_and_set_leave_everything_unchanged (refusal at the first connection and at the app secrets, plus the lost compare-and-set, each asserted against a whole-database dump taken before) and crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/secrets_key.rs::only_a_committed_replacement_earns_i24_and_a_refused_one_asks_again (the refused answer, the committed notice with its count, the lost compare-and-set). Both ran green in the reused smoke result. (d) Replace withheld and Start over offered with its cost under I-26: feature lines 1202-1375 drive the offer, the live-replica withholding, the stopped server, I-31 reading only I-31, the four I-28 counts, the replace door changing nothing under I-26, and the healthy key offering no start over. (e) Credentials it cannot open discarded, workspaces reconnect, the Slack app entered again: feature lines 1377-1409 assert the apply, the stored key this Foundry opens, the started-over activity line with its count, I-5 asking for the Slack app again, and Canzan Labs reading no connection as connected with Matrix offered and the shipped K-2 Slack words; 1414-1497 assert the trimmed confirmation, the wrong and empty confirmations changing nothing, the gate re-read inside the write when the other server speaks again, and the operator rotation after a start over; 1499-1549 assert the two orders of replace and start over. Every declared behaviour of the Request therefore has an executable stimulus and assertions that distinguish it from the plausible wrong behaviour named in the slice falsifiers. No coverage gap found; no finding with owner oracle.

diagnostic: Accepted, with two non-blocking implementation findings. The whole candidate at b61593f delivers the Request: Replace reads I-23 over the credentials stored now and replaces nothing until she confirms, the apply re-seals every stored value including the saved Slack app in one locked transaction with a compare-and-set on the stored key id, answers I-24 once through post-redirect-get and leaves no workspace reconnecting; a refused re-seal or a lost compare-and-set rolls everything back; under I-26 Replace is withheld and Start over is offered only while no replica with a fresh beat still opens the key and this server holds an instance key, I-28 states its cost with the I-28a typed confirmation, and the apply discards what this Foundry cannot open, records the count, leaves Canzan Labs told to set up again and asks for the Slack app again. Every declared behaviour has an executable stimulus and falsifying assertions (R6); the oracle needs no correction and no finding has owner oracle or product. Evidence: my own us-iis-07 lane run at the reviewed commit, exit 0, 29 of 29 scenarios and 513 of 513 steps, which is also the behaviour-preservation observation the rework commit lacked (R9); the host smoke run on bytes identical to b61593f, exit 0, all gates green, covering fmt, clippy, check-arch and the workspace suites that hold the store write tests and the handler and rotation library tests (R3); the port selector returned nothing inside its bound and is recorded as unusable tooling with a mechanical git fallback (R2). The three implementation findings of the earlier unpublished draft round are resolved and the rework touches no test path (R4). No test path was added or changed beyond the recorded oracle: the oracle and both supports change only in the acceptance designer's test commits, and the store test is the completion obligation the acceptance record itself assigns for the NotTested P3 (R7). No testing theatre found; the two strongest double-driven tests fail when the mapping or the rollback is removed. Open, non-blocking, owner implementation both: (1) the design's StartOverConfirmation carrier is absent, so the start-over apply is callable with no confirmation evidence and architecture.md:1704 claims a rustc-enforced exclusion the bytes do not give - behaviour is nonetheless observed correct at the public port; (2) answer() reads the replica states on every instance page render although only the Unopenable mode can use the answer. Limits retained: typesafe unavailable, TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent, no call made or fabricated and no producer judgment consumed (R8); import metadata unavailable, so exercised changed targets rest on the two runs above; no timing measurement was taken because no test is at half budget and no derogation is in force; and no peer address was discoverable from this role (no agent-listing tool), so both findings travel to the root for its owner.
